clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old male presented with cough and dyspnoea, which progressed over 5 weeks to include pleuritic chest pain and severe cough. A chest radiograph revealed a large mass in the right hemithorax. Subsequent CT imaging identified a 10x11 cm anterior mediastinal mass causing superior vena cava and pulmonary artery trunk stenosis, with no distant metastatic disease (clinical stage II). Histological evaluation of this mediastinal lesion confirmed an extragonadal germ cell tumour of yolk sac origin, supported by a significantly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein level of 17,000 ng/mL.
